summary: Radar for 2026-10-16 (GLP-1 focus). There are three fresh hooks today. (1) Europe's medicines committee (CHMP) recommended approval of Lilly's orforglipron pill (Foundayo) today. It will be the EU's second oral GLP-1 after the Wegovy pill. This is a named next-gen drug with a news peg, and that is our best-performing format. (2) Medscape and a Penn study (based on a medRxiv preprint) report that Reddit users of bootleg retatrutide most often describe increased appetite, fatigue and a racing heart. Those differ from the stomach-and-gut side effects that dominated the trials. This extends our best Short (bootleg 'Reta', 128 views) with an evergreen 'research peptide isn't the trial drug' angle. Counterfeit pens seized by the UK regulator (MHRA) and a photo study finding that about 26% of self-reported users were actually on compounded products reinforce that lane. (3) Fractyl reported today that its Revita device met its 6-month main goal in the REMAIN-1 trial: about 80% vs 67% of GLP-1 weight loss kept, against a sham procedure. This is company-reported, not peer-reviewed. It refreshes 'what happens after stopping tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-4)'. Use a named drug in the title, which is what the playbook says the weak stopping posts lacked. Our tirzepatide muscle series stays the strongest evergreen lane, refreshed by a new Nutrients review of protein and resistance training. Retatrutide decoders should build toward Lilly's Oct 29 earnings. NAION (the 'eye stroke' story) is peaking scare coverage about an approved drug, and our data shows that lands low, so it's rated low priority. The low-dose tirzepatide cohort and the anorexia-misuse stories were left out because they risk dosing or eating-disorder framing.

It's a named next-gen drug, our proven format (orforglipron long-form 23; named-drug Shorts median 98). Creator coverage of the EU decision is near zero so far.
